news.headline: IRS Audit Revenue Drops $3.5 Billion After Agency Fires the People Who Collect Money
news.summary: IRSが大規模な人員削減を行った結果、2025会計年度の査察による税収が35億ドル減少したことが、政府の監視機関の調査で明らかになった。

commentary: 矛盾: 税金を取り立てる職員を削減すると税収が減る——これ、誰でも予測できた話なんですよ。監視機関が「調査して発見しました」って言ってるけど、これ発見じゃなくて算数ですよね。
滑稽さ: 「政府の無駄を省く」という名目で、年間35億ドルを回収していた部署を削ったわけですよ。節約するために損してる。財布の穴を広げて「スリム化した」って言ってる感じ。
日本・海外から見ると: 日本だと国税庁の調査官を大量解雇して「財政健全化」と呼ぶ政権は想像しにくい。アメリカでは実際に起きて、監視機関が驚いた顔でレポートを出してるんですよ。
imagePrompts: A government office with rows of empty desks and "AUDITOR" nameplates left behind. A single remaining worker stares at a towering stack of unfiled tax returns. A whiteboard reads 'Savings: $0. Lost Revenue: $3,500,000,000.'

A large piggy bank with a label reading 'TAX REVENUE' sitting on a table. Next to it, a pair of scissors and a pile of pink slips from 'IRS Workforce Reduction.' The bank has a wide-open hole in the bottom.

A courtroom-style weigh scale: one side holds a stack of documents labeled 'AUDITOR SALARIES SAVED,' the other side is crushed under a boulder labeled '$3.5 BILLION UNCOLLECTED.' The scale is almost vertical.
captions: We fired the people who collect money to save money. The auditors are gone. The math, unfortunately, stayed.
The IRS lost $3.5 billion in audit revenue. Don't worry — a watchdog noticed. Six months later. In a report.
Firing your revenue collectors to cut costs: bold strategy. How'd that work out? Thirty-five hundred million dollars of 'not great.'
Somewhere, the auditors who got laid off are doing their taxes. And laughing.
You know your government efficiency plan has a flaw when the watchdog report title is basically 'We Checked, and Fewer Auditors Means Less Auditing.'
captionsJa: お金を集める人を削減してお金を節約しようとした。査察官は去った。算数は残った。
IRSは査察で35億ドル失った。大丈夫、監視機関が気づいた。半年後に。報告書で。
税収担当者を解雇してコスト削減。結果は？35億ドル分の「うまくいかなかった」。
解雇された査察官たち、今ごろ自分の確定申告をしながら笑ってると思う。
政府の効率化計画に欠陥があるとわかるサイン——監視機関レポートのタイトルが「査察官を減らしたら査察が減りました」のとき。
candidates.newsEn: A federal watchdog found that IRS audit revenue fell by $3.5 billion in fiscal year 2025 following significant workforce reductions at the agency. The IRS shed thousands of auditors and support staff as part of broader government downsizing efforts. The drop means billions in potentially owed taxes went uncollected during the period.

ironyEn.contradiction: The government cut the department responsible for collecting $3.5 billion in taxes and called it fiscal responsibility. That's not trimming the fat — that's cutting off the arm that holds the wallet.
ironyEn.absurdity: A watchdog had to write an official report to explain that firing auditors leads to fewer audits. Next quarter: watchdog discovers water is wet.
ironyEn.outside: Most countries treat tax enforcement as revenue-generating infrastructure. The U.S. apparently filed it under 'unnecessary overhead.'

ironyEn.contradiction: Agencies tasked with reducing government waste eliminated one of the few government functions that literally returns more money than it costs.
ironyEn.absurdity: The IRS lost 35 hundred million dollars in collections — not to fraud, not to a crash, but to a spreadsheet that said 'less staff = savings.'
ironyEn.outside: From abroad, this looks like a shop that fired all its cashiers to cut labor costs, then announced record losses at checkout.

news.headline: House Votes to Condemn Socialism — Also, Please Show Your ID to Vote
news.summary: 米下院は11月の中間選挙を前に社会主義を非難する決議案を採決にかけたが、共和党はその決議文の中に賛否が大きく割れる有権者ID法案（SAVE America Act）の可決要求も盛り込んだ。

commentary: 矛盾: 「社会主義反対」の決議文の中に、別の法案を通せという要求を忍び込ませるのは、デモクラシーの純粋なやつですよ。反社会主義を叫びながら、議会の手続きでちゃっかり抱き合わせ商法をやってるわけで。
滑稽さ: 「社会主義を非難する」という声明のためだけに投票するのかと思ったら、裏メニューがついてた。政治のセットメニュー——メインは理念、サイドに選挙制度改変、ドリンクは選択不可。
日本・海外から見ると: 選挙前に「社会主義はダメ」と全員で声を揃えて宣言する文化は、アメリカ特有のものがある。日本だと国会で「資本主義最高！賛成の方は挙手」という採決は想像しにくい。
imagePrompts: A large ornate congressional resolution document titled 'CONDEMNING SOCIALISM' with bold red text. At the bottom, in tiny fine print, is a paragraph titled 'Also, Voter ID Bill.' A magnifying glass is hovering over the fine print.

A restaurant menu titled 'DEMOCRACY COMBO MEAL.' Listed items: 'Anti-Socialism Statement (symbolic)' as the main, and 'SAVE America Act (highly contested)' as the mandatory side dish. No substitutions.
A politician at a podium holding a giant banner reading 'NO SOCIALISM' while a second, smaller sign quietly slides into frame from the side reading 'P.S. Voter ID Bill, please.'
captions: Congress voted to condemn socialism. Bundled inside: a voter-ID bill that couldn't pass on its own. Free-market principles, apparently, don't apply to legislation.
The resolution against socialism came with a surprise inside. Like a Kinder egg, but for electoral policy.
They needed a vote on whether socialism is bad. In 2026. Took the opportunity to sneak in another bill. Efficient use of everyone's time.
Anti-socialism resolution, featuring a bonus voting restriction — because nothing says 'land of freedom' like terms and conditions.
So the bill couldn't pass alone, so they stapled it to 'socialism bad.' At this point Congress is just doing what the rest of us do when we bury a question in the middle of a long text.
captionsJa: 議会は社会主義を非難する決議を採決した。その中に、単独では通らなかった投票制限法案が入っていた。自由市場の原理は、どうやら法案には適用されないらしい。
社会主義反対の決議に、サプライズ入り。キンダーエッグみたいなものだけど、中身は選挙制度。
2026年に、社会主義がダメかどうかの採決があった。ついでに別の法案を忍び込ませた。みんなの時間を有効活用。
反社会主義決議、特典として投票制限付き。「自由の国」が規約と条件付きになってきた。
単独で通らないから「社会主義はダメ」にくっつけた。長いLINEの真ん中にこっそり質問を混ぜる手法を、議会もやってるとは思わなかった。
candidates.newsEn: The U.S. House of Representatives voted on a resolution condemning socialism ahead of November's midterm elections. Republicans added language to the resolution calling for passage of the SAVE America Act, a controversial voter-ID bill that has faced significant opposition. The move bundled a broad ideological statement with a specific and contested piece of legislation.

ironyEn.contradiction: A resolution condemning ideological overreach was used to push through a separate, unrelated, and deeply contested policy goal. Democracy doing a little socialism of its own — sharing one bill's momentum with another.
ironyEn.absurdity: Congress took a stand against an economic system by hiding a voting-rights bill inside the stand. The anti-socialism package came bundled with extras, like a cable contract.
ironyEn.outside: Observers abroad may note that the U.S. Congress scheduled a formal vote on whether socialism is bad — roughly 35 years after the Cold War ended.

ironyEn.contradiction: The party that opposes government overreach used a government resolution to pressure passage of a separate government bill they couldn't pass on its own merits.
ironyEn.absurdity: Attaching a voter-ID mandate to an anti-socialism statement is a bit like putting a parking ticket in a birthday card. Technically valid. Still a weird move.
ironyEn.outside: Most legislatures save the ideological declarations for speeches. The U.S. House made it a vehicle for hitchhiking legislation.

news.headline: GoPro Is Pivoting to AI Data Centers. Its Stock Jumped 40%.
news.summary: アクションカメラメーカーのGoPro社が、フォトニクス企業Starman Opticalとの合併を発表し、AIデータセンター分野に参入すると表明。株価は40%急騰した。

commentary: 矛盾: スカイダイビングや波乗りの動画を撮るカメラを作っていた会社が、データセンターに転身する。ユーザーが「崖から飛んだ映像」を撮っていたら、会社のほうも崖から飛んだ——ただしAIという方向に。
滑稽さ: 「AI」とつけた途端に株が40%上がる市場が面白いんですよ。GoPro、もしかして今まで発表する言葉を間違えてただけでは？「サーフィン動画カメラ、AIデータセンターに転身」と言った瞬間に価値が生まれた。
日本・海外から見ると: 日本で言うと、ガラス工芸の会社が突然「AIクラウドインフラに参入します」と発表して株価が急騰するようなもの。業種の連続性ゼロ。でも市場は「AI」を聞いた瞬間に動く。
imagePrompts: A GoPro action camera mounted on a helmet, but instead of a skier on a mountain, the camera is strapped to a server rack in a sterile data center. Blinking LEDs everywhere. No mountains in sight.
A stock chart shaped like a cliff dive — flat for years, then a vertical 40% spike — displayed on a monitor in a server room. A GoPro camera sits on the desk next to a keyboard, gathering dust.

A trade show booth split down the middle: the left side shows GoPro's classic branding with surfers and skydivers; the right side has been hastily redecorated with AI data center imagery and a new logo still being hot-glued on.
captions: GoPro pivoted to AI data centers. Stock up 40%. The extreme sport now is telling investors what they want to hear.
The company that filmed people jumping off cliffs has announced it's jumping into AI infrastructure. Honestly, the risk tolerance tracks.
GoPro didn't build a new product. It just said 'AI data center' in a press release. Forty percent. That's the whole story.
Remember when GoPro was for people doing cool stuff outside? The new product is: server rooms. Still shoots great footage of nothing happening.
At what point do we admit the word 'AI' is just a financial energy drink? GoPro drank it. Up 40% before lunch.
captionsJa: GoPro、AIデータセンターに転身。株価40%上昇。今一番過激なスポーツは「投資家が聞きたいことを言う」こと。
崖から飛ぶ人を撮ってた会社が、AIインフラに飛び込んだ。リスク許容度は一貫してる、確かに。
GoPro、新製品は作ってない。プレスリリースに「AIデータセンター」と書いただけ。40%上昇。以上。
外でかっこいことする人向けのカメラ、覚えてますか？新商品はサーバールームです。映像は相変わらずきれいに撮れます、何も起きていない様子を。
「AI」という言葉が財務上のエナドリになってる時点でもう認めようよ。GoPro飲んだら昼前に40%上がった。
candidates.newsEn: GoPro, the maker of action cameras popular with extreme sports enthusiasts, announced a merger with private photonics company Starman Optical and a pivot into AI data center infrastructure. The company's shares surged approximately 40% on the news. The move represents a dramatic departure from GoPro's core consumer electronics business.

ironyEn.contradiction: A company whose entire identity was built on filming humans doing reckless things in physical space has announced its future is in server rooms. The camera that survived avalanches is now chasing data center margins.
ironyEn.absurdity: GoPro's stock jumped 40% not because it built anything new, but because it announced a merger and used the word 'AI.' The product hasn't changed. The ticker has.
ironyEn.outside: From outside the U.S., the GoPro story reads like a perfectly calibrated market experiment: say 'AI data center,' measure the spike, repeat.

ironyEn.contradiction: GoPro spent decades branding itself as the camera for people who do real, physical, dangerous things. Its pivot to data centers is about as on-brand as a skateboard company opening a law firm.
ironyEn.absurdity: A 40% stock surge for a merger between an action camera brand and a photonics startup most people can't name — the market is apparently very easily startled by the word 'AI.'
ironyEn.outside: Investors rewarded GoPro for announcing it would stop doing the thing it was known for. It's the financial equivalent of applauding someone for quitting their job.

news.headline: Pentagon's Top AI Policy Official Sold $25M in AI Stock While Overseeing AI Policy
news.summary: 米国防総省でAI政策を統括するエミール・マイケル氏が、同職に就いている間にAI企業Perplexityの株式を最大2500万ドル相当売却していたことが、財務開示書類の調査で明らかになった。

commentary: 矛盾: AI政策を決める人が、AI株で数十億円分の利益を得ている。利益相反という言葉の辞書に、このニュースの写真を載せてもいい。
滑稽さ: xAI株で24億円、Perplexity株で25億円——これ、AI政策の「成果」をどちらが受け取っているか、わかりやすすぎる。国防総省の判断が市場に与える影響と、本人の口座残高が同じ方向を向いている。
日本・海外から見ると: 日本の防衛省でIT調達を担う高官が、調達先候補の株を数十億円分売却していたら——想像するだけで制度が震える。アメリカでは「開示したから問題ない」という建付けで動いている。
imagePrompts: A Pentagon briefing room table, shot from above. One side holds a stack of documents labeled 'AI ACQUISITION POLICY.' The other side holds a laptop open to a brokerage screen showing a trade confirmation for $25,000,000. A Pentagon ID badge sits face-down between them. No faces visible.

A large scale of justice. On one side: a Pentagon badge labeled 'AI POLICY OVERSIGHT.' On the other side: two bags of money labeled 'xAI $24M' and 'Perplexity $25M.' The scale is completely horizontal, perfectly balanced.

A conflict-of-interest flowchart on a whiteboard: 'Write AI policy' → 'AI companies gain value' → 'Sell AI stock' → 'File disclosure form' → arrow looping back to 'Write AI policy.' A smiley face drawn at the end.
captions: The Pentagon's top AI policy guy sold $25 million in AI stock. But he filed the disclosure. So we're good. We're totally good.
xAI: $24 million. Perplexity: $25 million. Job title: Pentagon AI Oversight. Resume's looking strong.
He's in charge of deciding which AI companies the military buys from. He's also very personally invested in how that goes.
Conflict of interest? No, no — he disclosed it. The form is filed. The $49 million is in the account. Oversight achieved.
You know how referees aren't supposed to bet on the game? The Pentagon would like to present a different perspective on that.
captionsJa: 国防総省のAI政策責任者がAI株を2500万ドル売却。でも開示書類は提出した。だから大丈夫。全然大丈夫。
xAI株で24億円、Perplexity株で25億円。肩書：国防総省AI監督官。職歴、充実してる。
軍がどのAI企業から買うか決める立場の人が、その結果に個人的にとても深く関心を持っている。
利益相反？いや、開示したから問題ないんですよ。書類は提出済み。49億円は口座に入ってる。監督完了。
審判が試合に賭けちゃいけないのはご存知の通り。国防総省はその件について、別の見解を持っているようです。
candidates.newsEn: Financial disclosures reviewed by The Guardian show that Emil Michael, the top Pentagon official responsible for overseeing military artificial intelligence policy, sold stock in AI company Perplexity worth up to $25 million. Michael had also previously reaped up to $24 million from selling xAI stock earlier this year. The official is responsible for shaping the military's AI acquisition and policy decisions.

ironyEn.contradiction: The official deciding which AI companies get Pentagon contracts held tens of millions of dollars in AI company stocks. The conflict of interest didn't need a microscope — it needed a brokerage statement.
ironyEn.absurdity: He sold $25 million in Perplexity stock and $24 million in xAI stock while writing national AI policy. At that point, 'oversight' is doing a lot of heavy lifting as a word.
ironyEn.outside: In most democracies, this level of financial entanglement between a regulator and the regulated industry would trigger automatic recusal. In Washington, it triggered a disclosure form.

ironyEn.contradiction: Emil Michael was in charge of making sure the military's AI investments serve the public interest — while personally earning $49 million from AI investments of his own.
ironyEn.absurdity: The Pentagon has an AI safety policy. The man who runs it made $25 million selling AI stock. 'Safety' is a flexible concept.
ironyEn.outside: The structure here is elegant in its simplicity: shape the policy, hold the stock, sell the stock, file the disclosure. All legal. All disclosed. All a bit much.

news.headline: USPS Is Launching a New Computer System That Could Derail Mail-In Voting. It's Due Before the Election.
news.summary: 民主党上院議員が内部告発者の声明を公開し、USPSが選挙前に導入予定の新コンピュータシステムが郵便投票に混乱をもたらす恐れがあると警告していることが明らかになった。チャック・シューマー上院議員はシステム導入を差し止める法案を提出した。

commentary: 矛盾: 郵便局が選挙直前に大規模なシステム移行を行う——IT業界なら「選挙期間中だけはシステム更新を止める」のが常識なのに、USPSはそのタイミングを選んでいるわけですよ。「フリーズ期間」が存在しないシステム運用。
滑稽さ: 内部告発者が「これはまずい」と言い、上院議員が「止めるための法案を出す」と言い、それでもシステムは予定通り動こうとしている。三者全員が違う方向に走っていて、誰も郵便物の行方を知らない状態になってきた。
日本・海外から見ると: 日本だと選挙管理の信頼性は「当然のインフラ」として扱われる。アメリカでは選挙の仕組み自体が毎回、政治的な争点になる。郵便局のシステム更新ですら国会審議になる国。
imagePrompts: A U.S. Postal Service worker standing in front of a massive server being wheeled through a sorting facility. Thousands of envelopes labeled 'BALLOT' are stacked everywhere. A calendar on the wall shows Election Day circled in red, just weeks away. A technician nearby holds a laptop showing 'SYSTEM MIGRATION IN PROGRESS.'

A flowchart on a whiteboard labeled 'MAIL-IN VOTING PROCESS.' Every arrow leads through a box labeled 'NEW USPS COMPUTER SYSTEM (UNTESTED)' surrounded by question marks. The final box just reads '???'

A split image: on the left, a voter carefully sealing a mail-in ballot envelope. On the right, the same envelope entering a sorting machine with a screen showing 'ERROR: SYSTEM UPDATING. PLEASE WAIT.'
captions: The post office is installing a new computer system before the election. The whistleblower says it could cause chaos. USPS says it'll be fine. Somewhere, a ballot is already nervous.
Nothing says 'democracy is working' like a Senate bill to stop the post office from doing an IT upgrade in October.
Mail-in voting: designed to be reliable. New USPS computer system: scheduled, untested, launching before November. These two facts are in a room together now.
The system that processes your ballot is getting a complete software overhaul six weeks before Election Day. Updates may take longer than expected. Please do not turn off your democracy.

A whistleblower warned the USPS system could derail mail-in voting. USPS said they're proceeding. Congress introduced a bill. The system is still being installed. Classic four-way standoff where the computers are winning.
captionsJa: 郵便局が選挙前に新しいコンピュータシステムを入れようとしている。内部告発者は「混乱が起きる」と言う。USPSは「大丈夫」と言う。どこかで投票用紙がもう不安になってる。
「郵便局が10月にシステム更新するのを止めるための法案」が上院で提出される——これ、民主主義が機能してる証拠としてカウントされるんですかね。
郵便投票は「信頼できる」設計のはず。USPSの新システムは未テストで、11月前に導入予定。この二つが今、同じ部屋にいる。
あなたの投票用紙を処理するシステムが、選挙の6週間前に全面ソフトウェア更新中です。更新には予想より時間がかかる場合があります。民主主義の電源は切らないでください。
内部告発者が警告し、議会が法案を出し、USPSは続行すると言い、システムはそのまま稼働している。四者四様のにらみ合い——今のところコンピュータが勝ってる。
candidates.newsEn: A Democratic senator disclosed a whistleblower statement warning that the U.S. Postal Service is set to launch a new computer system that could disrupt mail-in voting before November's midterm elections. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer introduced a bill that would block the rollout. The USPS system overhaul is moving forward despite the warnings, according to the disclosure.

ironyEn.contradiction: The U.S. Postal Service chose the months immediately before a national election to roll out a brand-new, untested computer system that handles mail sorting — including mail-in ballots. The timing was apparently not flagged as a concern until a whistleblower flagged it as a concern.
ironyEn.absurdity: A senator had to introduce a bill to stop the post office from upgrading its computers right before an election. That sentence should not exist.
ironyEn.outside: In countries with centralized election infrastructure, a last-minute IT overhaul at the national mail agency before voting day would be front-page news for weeks. Here, it surfaced in a whistleblower disclosure.

ironyEn.contradiction: Mail-in voting exists to make voting more accessible. The system being installed before the election could make mail-in voting less reliable. Infrastructure meant to expand access may end up narrowing it — accidentally, officially, on schedule.
ironyEn.absurdity: The whistleblower said the rollout could cause 'chaos.' USPS said it's moving forward. Congress is now in the position of trying to stop the post office from doing its own IT project.
ironyEn.outside: The U.S. debates whether mail-in voting is safe — then schedules a potentially destabilizing system upgrade right before an election that will rely on mail-in voting. The debate may be settling itself.

editorial.thread: 今日の5本を貫く糸：「やるべきことと逆のことを、自信満々でやる人たちの話」。IRS・議会・GoPro・国防総省・郵便局、全員が同じ方向に走っている。
editorial.titleEn: We Fired the Tax Collectors to Save Money. Guess What Happened.
editorial.subtitleEn: Five stories about doing the wrong thing with complete confidence.
editorial.titleJa: IRSが税金の取り立て係を解雇して35億ドル損した話と、その他4本
titleAltJa: 「AI」と言った瞬間に株が40%上がる市場で、ペンタゴンのAI担当が2500万ドル稼いでいた
今日のアメリカのニュース、全部「それって逆じゃないの」で返せる
editorial.leadJa:
算数の話を5本読みました。引き算を「改革」って呼んでる人たちの話です。

全部、ちゃんとした顔をして実行されています。
editorial.introEn:
I want to be clear: today's five stories are not complicated.

The IRS fired the people who collect money, and collected less money. The Pentagon's AI czar sold tens of millions in AI stock while running AI policy. GoPro said 'data center' in a press release and watched its stock jump 40%. Congress snuck a voter-ID bill inside a resolution about socialism. And the post office is installing a new computer system right before the election, while a whistleblower says please, please don't.

This is not chaos. This is the system doing exactly what it's set up to do — just not for you.

Which means your judgment is fine. If something about your week felt backwards, today's news is telling you: it probably was. Trust that instinct. You're reading the room correctly.
editorial.introJa:
35億ドル。

それが、「節約のために税金の取り立て係を解雇した」結果、消えた金額です。監視機関がレポートを出して「発見した」と言っています。いや、これ発見じゃなくて算数ですよね。

今日はそういう5本です。GoPro（スカイダイビング動画のカメラ会社）が「AIデータセンターに転身」と言って株価が40%上がった話。国防総省でAI政策を仕切る人が、AI株を25億円分売っていた話。あと、郵便局が選挙直前に新しいコンピュータシステムを入れようとしていて、内部告発者が止めてくれと言っている話。

5本全部、逆のことを自信満々でやっている人たちの話です。

今日の占いです。「なんかうまくいかない」と感じているなら、あなたのせいじゃないかもしれない。算数を無視して走っている人たちが、今日もいます。あなたはちゃんと数えられている。それだけで、今日はわりと大丈夫だと思う。
editorial.quipEn: Today's theme: doing the wrong thing, on purpose, with paperwork. The math didn't change. The outcomes were very predictable. And yet.
editorial.quipJa: 節約のために損して、利益相反を「開示したから問題なし」と言って、「AI」と言うだけで株が上がる。算数は壊れていない。使う人を選んでいるだけ。

editorial.fullEn:
# We Fired the Tax Collectors to Save Money. Guess What Happened.

## Today's Forecast

I want to be clear: today's five stories are not complicated.

The IRS fired the people who collect money, and collected less money. The Pentagon's AI czar sold tens of millions in AI stock while running AI policy. GoPro said 'data center' in a press release and watched its stock jump 40%. Congress snuck a voter-ID bill inside a resolution about socialism. And the post office is installing a new computer system right before the election, while a whistleblower says please, please don't.

This is not chaos. This is the system doing exactly what it's set up to do — just not for you.

Which means your judgment is fine. If something about your week felt backwards, today's news is telling you: it probably was. Trust that instinct. You're reading the room correctly.

---

## 1. IRS Audit Revenue Drops $3.5 Billion After Agency Fires the People Who Collect Money

*CBS News US — [source](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/irs-audit-revenue-decline-worker-cuts/)*

A federal watchdog found that IRS audit revenue fell by $3.5 billion in fiscal year 2025 following significant workforce reductions at the agency. The IRS shed thousands of auditors and support staff as part of broader government downsizing efforts. The drop means billions in potentially owed taxes went uncollected during the period.

**Why It's Funny**

The IRS let go of thousands of auditors. Audit revenue dropped $3.5 billion. A federal watchdog looked into it and published a report calling this a 'finding.' I want to be precise about what they found: they found that when you stop collecting money, you collect less money. This is not investigative journalism. This is a subtraction problem that got a government letterhead. The auditors are gone. The math, unfortunately, stayed.

**Say It Out Loud**

> We fired the people who collect money to save money. The auditors are gone. The math, unfortunately, stayed.

---

## 2. House Votes to Condemn Socialism — Also, Please Show Your ID to Vote

*CNBC Top News — [source](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/01/congress-vote-condemning-socialism-election.html)*

The U.S. House of Representatives voted on a resolution condemning socialism ahead of November's midterm elections. Republicans added language to the resolution calling for passage of the SAVE America Act, a controversial voter-ID bill that has faced significant opposition. The move bundled a broad ideological statement with a specific and contested piece of legislation.

**Why It's Funny**

The House voted to condemn socialism. Simple enough. But Republicans added language to the resolution pushing for a voter-ID bill — one that had been struggling to pass on its own. So the anti-socialism statement came with a bonus item tucked inside, like terms and conditions nobody reads. They needed a moral declaration to carry the legislation across the finish line. Free-market principles, apparently, don't apply to how you move legislation.

**Say It Out Loud**

> Congress voted to condemn socialism. Bundled inside: a voter-ID bill that couldn't pass on its own. Free-market principles, apparently, don't apply to legislation.

---

## 3. GoPro Is Pivoting to AI Data Centers. Its Stock Jumped 40%.

*CNBC Top News — [source](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/01/gopro-stock-ai-data-centers.html)*

GoPro, the maker of action cameras popular with extreme sports enthusiasts, announced a merger with private photonics company Starman Optical and a pivot into AI data center infrastructure. The company's shares surged approximately 40% on the news. The move represents a dramatic departure from GoPro's core consumer electronics business.

**Why It's Funny**

GoPro — the company whose whole identity is strapping a camera to someone who is about to do something inadvisable — announced it's merging with a photonics firm and pivoting to AI data centers. The stock jumped 40%. No new product. No prototype. A press release with the words 'AI' and 'data center' in it. The extreme sport turned out to be investor relations.

**Say It Out Loud**

> GoPro pivoted to AI data centers. Stock up 40%. The extreme sport now is telling investors what they want to hear.

---

## 4. Pentagon's Top AI Policy Official Sold $25M in AI Stock While Overseeing AI Policy

*The Guardian US — [source](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/01/top-pentagon-official-ai-stock-holdings)*

Financial disclosures reviewed by The Guardian show that Emil Michael, the top Pentagon official responsible for overseeing military artificial intelligence policy, sold stock in AI company Perplexity worth up to $25 million. Michael had also previously reaped up to $24 million from selling xAI stock earlier this year. The official is responsible for shaping the military's AI acquisition and policy decisions.

**Why It's Funny**

Emil Michael oversees AI policy at the Pentagon — which companies the military works with, what gets funded, how the whole thing is shaped. He also sold up to $25 million in Perplexity stock while doing that job. Earlier this year: up to $24 million from xAI. He filed disclosures. Everything is technically above board. The word 'technically' is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

**Say It Out Loud**

> The Pentagon's top AI policy guy sold $25 million in AI stock. But he filed the disclosure. So we're good. We're totally good.

---

## 5. USPS Is Launching a New Computer System That Could Derail Mail-In Voting. It's Due Before the Election.

*The Guardian US — [source](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/sep/01/house-vote-stopgap-funding-bill-us-federal-government-shutdown-mike-johnson-trump-ballroom-politics-latest-news-updates)*

A Democratic senator disclosed a whistleblower statement warning that the U.S. Postal Service is set to launch a new computer system that could disrupt mail-in voting before November's midterm elections. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer introduced a bill that would block the rollout. The USPS system overhaul is moving forward despite the warnings, according to the disclosure.

**Why It's Funny**

The USPS is launching a new computer system before November's midterm elections. A whistleblower says it could disrupt mail-in voting. Chuck Schumer introduced a bill to stop the rollout. The rollout is continuing anyway. Three separate people are running in three separate directions, and somewhere in the middle of all this is a ballot that just wants to arrive on time.

**Say It Out Loud**

> The post office is installing a new computer system before the election. The whistleblower says it could cause chaos. USPS says it'll be fine. Somewhere, a ballot is already nervous.

---

## Today's Punchline

> Today's theme: doing the wrong thing, on purpose, with paperwork. The math didn't change. The outcomes were very predictable. And yet.
editorial.fullJa:
# IRSが税金の取り立て係を解雇して35億ドル損した話と、その他4本

## 今日を占うよ〜

35億ドル。

それが、「節約のために税金の取り立て係を解雇した」結果、消えた金額です。監視機関がレポートを出して「発見した」と言っています。いや、これ発見じゃなくて算数ですよね。

今日はそういう5本です。GoPro（スカイダイビング動画のカメラ会社）が「AIデータセンターに転身」と言って株価が40%上がった話。国防総省でAI政策を仕切る人が、AI株を25億円分売っていた話。あと、郵便局が選挙直前に新しいコンピュータシステムを入れようとしていて、内部告発者が止めてくれと言っている話。

5本全部、逆のことを自信満々でやっている人たちの話です。

今日の占いです。「なんかうまくいかない」と感じているなら、あなたのせいじゃないかもしれない。算数を無視して走っている人たちが、今日もいます。あなたはちゃんと数えられている。それだけで、今日はわりと大丈夫だと思う。

---

## 1. IRS Audit Revenue Drops $3.5 Billion After Agency Fires the People Who Collect Money

*CBS News US（[記事](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/irs-audit-revenue-decline-worker-cuts/)）*

IRSが大規模な人員削減を行った結果、2025会計年度の査察による税収が35億ドル減少したことが、政府の監視機関の調査で明らかになった。

**どこが笑える？**

税金を取り立てる調査官を大量解雇したら、査察による税収が35億ドル減りました。政府の監視機関がこれを調査して、報告書にまとめて「発見した」と言っています。

待って。これ発見じゃないですよ。引き算です。調査官がいなくなれば査察が減る。査察が減れば取りこぼす税金が増える。誰でも予測できる話を、政府機関が半年かけて確認してレポートにした。

調査官は消えました。算数だけが残っています。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> お金を集める人を削減してお金を節約しようとした。査察官は去った。算数は残った。

---

## 2. House Votes to Condemn Socialism — Also, Please Show Your ID to Vote

*CNBC Top News（[記事](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/01/congress-vote-condemning-socialism-election.html)）*

米下院は11月の中間選挙を前に社会主義を非難する決議案を採決にかけたが、共和党はその決議文の中に賛否が大きく割れる有権者ID法案（SAVE America Act）の可決要求も盛り込んだ。

**どこが笑える？**

「社会主義を非難する決議」を下院で採決しました。まあ、それはいい。問題は決議文の中に、単独では通る見込みの薄い有権者ID法案の可決要求が盛り込まれていたことです。

メインディッシュは理念。サイドに選挙制度改変。ドリンクは選べません。

「社会主義はダメ」に全員が手を挙げたタイミングで、裏メニューが通る仕組みになっていた。自由市場の原理、どうやら議会の手続きには適用されないらしい。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 議会は社会主義を非難する決議を採決した。その中に、単独では通らなかった投票制限法案が入っていた。自由市場の原理は、どうやら法案には適用されないらしい。

---

## 3. GoPro Is Pivoting to AI Data Centers. Its Stock Jumped 40%.

*CNBC Top News（[記事](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/01/gopro-stock-ai-data-centers.html)）*

アクションカメラメーカーのGoPro社が、フォトニクス企業Starman Opticalとの合併を発表し、AIデータセンター分野に参入すると表明。株価は40%急騰した。

**どこが笑える？**

GoProはスカイダイビングや波乗りの動画を撮るカメラの会社です。その会社が今週、フォトニクス企業と合併してAIデータセンター分野に参入すると発表しました。

株価が40%上がりました。

新製品は出ていません。プレスリリースに「AI」と「データセンター」と書いた。それだけで価値が40%増えた。もしかしてGoPro、ずっと発表する言葉を間違えていただけでは。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> GoPro、AIデータセンターに転身。株価40%上昇。今一番過激なスポーツは「投資家が聞きたいことを言う」こと。

---

## 4. Pentagon's Top AI Policy Official Sold $25M in AI Stock While Overseeing AI Policy

*The Guardian US（[記事](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/01/top-pentagon-official-ai-stock-holdings)）*

米国防総省でAI政策を統括するエミール・マイケル氏が、同職に就いている間にAI企業Perplexityの株式を最大2500万ドル相当売却していたことが、財務開示書類の調査で明らかになった。

**どこが笑える？**

エミール・マイケル氏は米国防総省でAI政策を統括しています。どのAI企業を軍が使うか、どこに予算がつくか、そういうことを決める立場です。

その人が、在職中にPerplexityの株を最大2500万ドル売却していました。今年初めにはxAI株でも最大2400万ドル。財務開示はしています。なので制度的には問題ないらしい。

「開示したから問題ない」。その一文、何回読んでも慣れないな。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 国防総省のAI政策責任者がAI株を2500万ドル売却。でも開示書類は提出した。だから大丈夫。全然大丈夫。

---

## 5. USPS Is Launching a New Computer System That Could Derail Mail-In Voting. It's Due Before the Election.

*The Guardian US（[記事](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/sep/01/house-vote-stopgap-funding-bill-us-federal-government-shutdown-mike-johnson-trump-ballroom-politics-latest-news-updates)）*

民主党上院議員が内部告発者の声明を公開し、USPSが選挙前に導入予定の新コンピュータシステムが郵便投票に混乱をもたらす恐れがあると警告していることが明らかになった。チャック・シューマー上院議員はシステム導入を差し止める法案を提出した。

**どこが笑える？**

郵便局が、11月の選挙の前に新しいコンピュータシステムを導入しようとしています。内部告発者が「郵便投票に混乱が起きる」と警告しています。上院の野党トップが差し止め法案を出しています。それでもシステムは予定通り進んでいます。

止めようとしてる人が二人いて、止まらない。そういう話です。どこかの投票用紙が、今からすでに不安そうにしています。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 郵便局が選挙前に新しいコンピュータシステムを入れようとしている。内部告発者は「混乱が起きる」と言う。USPSは「大丈夫」と言う。どこかで投票用紙がもう不安になってる。

---

## 今日のまとめジョーク/パンチライン

> 節約のために損して、利益相反を「開示したから問題なし」と言って、「AI」と言うだけで株が上がる。算数は壊れていない。使う人を選んでいるだけ。

今日も読んでくれてありがとうございます。また明日の朝、ここで。
editorial.reviewNotes: d4のimagePrompts[0]が実在人物（エミール・マイケル氏）を特定可能な形で描写しており権利・類似リスクがある。その他のcaptions・imagePromptsは合格水準。editorial全体はペルソナ・文体・SNS単体成立とも問題なし。d4のimagePrompts一本のみ修正。 ／ 文体パス: 3箇所修正。leadJaの「足し算ではなく、引き算を『改革』と呼んでいる人たちの話です」が説明口調でプレゼンっぽかったので崩した。riffJa[3]の「財務開示はしています。なので制度的には問題ないらしい」は合格だが末尾の「すごく長い距離を走っています」が気の利いた締め感があったので本音がこぼれる形に。riffJa[4]の「三者が三方向に走っていて、誰も郵便物の行方を知らない状態になってきた」が整いすぎた総括だったので崩した。
